categoryName: Spices, masalas, salt, sugar, jaggery, cooking essentials

skuLines.line: Turmeric powder (haldi) — everyday mass grade
skuLines.examples: Everest Turmeric, MDH Haldi, Patanjali Haldi, Goldiee Haldi
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; small lift in winter (haldi doodh)
skuLines.notes: Highest-penetration spice in India — never out of stock. Hygroscopic: cakes fast above 55-60% RH, so keep off the floor, pallet-stacked, and prefer poly/laminate over paper in monsoon.

skuLines.line: Turmeric powder — premium / single-origin, high-curcumin
skuLines.examples: Tata Sampann Turmeric (natural oils), 24 Mantra Organic Haldi, Lakadong / Salem turmeric, Pro Nature Organic
skuLines.notes: Clean-label is now a baseline expectation, not a premium claim (2026). One premium facing per powder is enough — don't build a second premium tier in a captive 5,000-person market.

skuLines.line: Red chilli powder (lal mirch) — everyday hot
skuLines.examples: Everest Tikhalal, MDH Lal Mirch, Catch Red Chilli, Goldiee Mirch
skuLines.notes: Stock two heat levels — a hostel/canteen kitchen feeding children 5-18 buys mild, staff families buy hot. Colour fades in light: keep out of window display.

skuLines.line: Kashmiri / Deggi Mirch chilli powder — colour, low heat
skuLines.examples: MDH Deggi Mirch, Everest Kashmiri Lal, Catch Kashmiri Chilli
skuLines.notes: The colour-without-heat SKU children's food and paneer dishes need. Verified retail: MDH Deggi Mirch 100 g ~₹115-125 (Aug 2026).

skuLines.line: Coriander powder (dhania) and dhania-jeera blend
skuLines.examples: Everest Dhania Powder, Tata Sampann Coriander, MDH Dhania, Vasant Coriander
skuLines.notes: Highest-volume powder after haldi/mirch; the 500 g and 1 kg packs are what married-staff kitchens actually buy. Ground coriander loses aroma in ~6 months — rotate FIFO.

skuLines.line: Cumin powder (jeera powder)
skuLines.examples: Everest Jeera Powder, MDH Jeeravan/Jeera, Catch Cumin Powder
skuLines.notes: Jeera is the most price-volatile mainstream spice (wholesale has swung 2x-3x across 2023-2026) — re-check the landed cost every indent rather than holding an MRP.

skuLines.line: Black pepper powder + table sprinkler
skuLines.examples: Catch Black Pepper Sprinkler, Everest Kali Mirch Powder, Keya Black Pepper
skuLines.notes: Cold hill winters drive kali mirch + sonth + tulsi kadha demand. The sprinkler pack is a canteen/table SKU, the pouch is a kitchen SKU — carry both.

skuLines.line: Amchur (dry mango powder)
skuLines.examples: Everest Amchur, MDH Amchur, Pushp Amchur
skuLines.notes: Named explicitly in pahari cooking (with haldi, hing, panch phoran, tej patta) — not an optional 'north Indian extra' here.

skuLines.line: Asafoetida (hing) — compounded and strong grade
skuLines.examples: Vandevi Hing, LG Hing, Ramdev Hing, Pushp Shahi Hing, Bandhani/Dabur
skuLines.notes: Two demand streams: pahari daily cooking, and infant/toddler dal for gas relief. Airtight only — hing perfumes every pack near it, so shelve it away from tea, milk powder and biscuits.

skuLines.line: Supporting powders — dry ginger (sonth), kasuri methi, garlic/onion powder
skuLines.examples: Everest Kasuri Methi, MDH Kasoori Methi, Zandu/local sonth, Keya Garlic Powder
skuLines.packSizes: kasuri methi 25 g / 100 g; sonth 100 g; garlic powder 50-100 g
skuLines.priceBand: ₹25-45 /25 g kasuri methi; ₹60-110 /100 g sonth; ₹60-120 /100 g garlic powder
skuLines.notes: Sonth is a winter hill essential and also goes into post-natal panjiri for married staff — stock deeper Oct-Jan. Garlic/onion powder is mainly a canteen buy.

skuLines.line: Anardana (dried pomegranate) — whole and powder
skuLines.examples: Local Sirmaur/Chamba anardana (loose), Pushp Anardana, Nature's Own
skuLines.seasonality: local harvest Sep-Nov; buy the year's stock then
skuLines.notes: The signature Himachali souring agent (chicken anardana, pahari chutney) — a national-brand-only spice rack will look wrong to Sirmauri staff. Best sourced locally, which also cuts hill freight.

skuLines.line: Cumin seeds whole (jeera)
skuLines.examples: Tata Sampann Jeera, Everest Jeera Whole, loose Unjha jeera
skuLines.packSizes: 100 g, 200 g, 500 g; loose by gram
skuLines.notes: Whole spices hold aroma 18-24 months vs 6-12 for ground — in a store 30-50 km from resupply, whole is the safer inventory bet and lets residents grind to need.

skuLines.line: Coriander seeds whole (sabut dhania)
skuLines.examples: Loose Rajasthan/MP dhania, Tata Sampann Coriander Whole
skuLines.notes: Cheap, slow-spoiling, high-rotation — a natural anchor for the loose weighed counter.

skuLines.line: Mustard seeds (rai / sarson) — black and yellow
skuLines.examples: Loose black rai, Everest Rai, yellow sarson (pickling grade)
skuLines.notes: Pahari cooking is mustard-led (auriya kaddu, mustard-oil tempering) plus every household's summer achar — carry yellow (coarse, for pickle) separately from black (tempering).

skuLines.line: Methi dana (fenugreek seeds) and ajwain (carom seeds)
skuLines.examples: Loose methi dana, Everest Ajwain, Tata Sampann Ajwain
skuLines.seasonality: methi Nov-Feb (winter laddoo) and Apr-Jun (pickle); ajwain year-round
skuLines.notes: Ajwain is the single most-asked item by mothers of infants (ajwain water for colic) — a store serving married staff families with babies cannot run out. Keep a small 50 g pack for that use.

skuLines.line: Fennel (saunf) — cooking grade and mukhwas/sugar-coated
skuLines.examples: Loose Lucknowi saunf, Everest Saunf, Chandan Mukhwas, sugar-coated (mishri) saunf
skuLines.notes: Double-duty: cooking spice plus after-meal mouth freshener — and in a tobacco-free township mukhwas/saunf is the substitute habit, so it over-indexes here.

skuLines.line: Whole dry red chillies (sabut lal mirch)
skuLines.examples: Loose Guntur (hot), Byadgi/Kashmiri (colour), Everest whole chilli
skuLines.seasonality: buy at Feb-Apr harvest; grind-to-order peaks pre-monsoon
skuLines.notes: Many hill households still buy whole chilli and have it ground — pair this line with an in-store grinding service (see adjacent services). Store dry; whole chilli mildews fast in monsoon.

skuLines.line: Black peppercorns whole (sabut kali mirch)
skuLines.examples: Loose Malabar/Wayanad pepper, Tata Sampann Black Pepper Whole
skuLines.notes: High value per gram — keep behind the counter. Price is volatile (Malabar pepper has moved 30-50% in a year); re-price each indent, don't inherit an old MRP.

skuLines.line: Green cardamom (choti elaichi)
skuLines.examples: Loose Idukki/Alleppey elaichi, Everest Elaichi, Catch Cardamom
skuLines.seasonality: spikes at Gurpurabs, Baisakhi, Diwali/Bandi Chhor (prasad, kheer, sweets)
skuLines.notes: Highest-shrink item in the category: sell in 10 g and 25 g packs at the counter, not open shelf. Festival prasad and tea both pull on it, so demand is lumpy around the Sikh calendar.

skuLines.line: Whole garam masala spices — laung, dalchini, tej patta, badi elaichi, jaiphal-javitri, star anise
skuLines.examples: Loose cloves, cassia/dalchini, bay leaf, black cardamom; Everest / Pushp whole packs
skuLines.priceBand: ₹20-40 /50 g tej patta; ₹30-70 /100 g dalchini; ₹120-230 /100 g laung; ₹150-300 /100 g jaiphal
skuLines.notes: One buying decision, six SKUs — a 6-jar whole-garam-masala block on the loose counter covers pahari and Punjabi cooking and lets residents make their own blend, which many hill families prefer.

skuLines.line: Sesame (til), kalonji and poppy (khus khus) seeds
skuLines.examples: Loose white/black til, Everest Kalonji, khus khus (loose)
skuLines.seasonality: til spikes hard for Lohri/Maghi (13-14 Jan) — gur-til, revri, tilkut
skuLines.notes: Lohri and Maghi are major dates in a Punjabi-Sikh township: til + gur move together in Dec-Jan and should be indented as a pair. Poppy seed is a controlled commodity — keep purchase invoices for every lot.

skuLines.line: Tamarind (imli) — seedless block and paste/concentrate
skuLines.examples: Loose seedless imli, Dabur Hommade Tamarind Paste, Tata Sampann Imli
skuLines.notes: Also the base for the South Indian staff/student contingent (sambar, rasam). Block imli sweats and moulds in monsoon — buy small and often, or stock paste through Jul-Sep.

skuLines.line: Saffron (kesar)
skuLines.examples: Baby Brand Kesar, Lion Dates Saffron, Kashmiri Mongra (loose/branded), Upakarma
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurabs, weddings, winter (kesar doodh), and post-natal diets
skuLines.notes: Low units, high ticket — one branded 1 g facing plus one 2 g is enough. Counter-locked; adulteration complaints are reputational in a closed community, so buy only branded/lab-tested lots.

skuLines.line: Dry coconut (copra gola) and desiccated coconut powder
skuLines.examples: Loose copra halves, Sri Sri/Anmol desiccated coconut, Nutraj
skuLines.seasonality: festival and prasad peaks; year-round for sweets
skuLines.notes: Used in prasad, langar sweets, chutney and South Indian cooking. Copra turns rancid above ~25°C with humidity — small lots, and don't hold it through the monsoon.

skuLines.line: Garam masala — mass and premium facings
skuLines.examples: Everest Garam Masala, MDH Garam Masala, Catch (low-temp ground), Pushp Punjabi Garam Masala
skuLines.notes: Verified retail Aug 2026: Everest 100 g ~₹92-100, MDH ~₹110. Carry a Punjabi-style regional blend alongside the two nationals — the top five national brands are together under 30% of the Indian market, and regional taste wins in a Punjabi-majority institution.

skuLines.line: Pulse-dish masalas — chole/chana, rajma, dal makhani
skuLines.examples: MDH Chana Masala, Everest Chhole Masala, MDH Dal Makhani Masala, Aachi Chana Masala
skuLines.notes: Chole and rajma are the backbone of vegetarian Punjabi cooking and of langar-style catering — these move like single spices here, not like specialty blends.

skuLines.line: Kitchen King / all-purpose sabji masala
skuLines.examples: MDH Kitchen King, Tata Sampann Kitchen King, Everest Sabji Masala, Badshah
skuLines.notes: Verified: Tata Sampann Kitchen King 100 g ~₹83. The one-jar shortcut for staff couples who both work and cook late — the highest-repeat blend after garam masala.

skuLines.line: Street-food masalas — chaat masala, pani puri masala, jaljeera
skuLines.examples: Everest Chaat Masala, MDH Chunky Chat, Badshah Pav Bhaji/Chaat, Everest Pani Puri Masala 50 g
skuLines.seasonality: Apr-Jun peak (jaljeera, aam panna); event/fair spikes
skuLines.notes: This is the canteen and youth line — 5,000 residents of whom most are 5-25 years old means chaat/pani-puri demand runs through the two canteens as well as households.

skuLines.line: Pav bhaji masala
skuLines.examples: Everest Pav Bhaji Masala 100 g, Badshah Pav Bhaji, MDH Pav Bhaji
skuLines.notes: Everest's single largest blend nationally and a canteen mainstay. Demand is tied to the academic term, not the calendar — cut the indent during winter/summer break when students go home.

skuLines.line: Biryani and pulao masala
skuLines.examples: Everest Shahi Biryani Masala, MDH Biryani, Aachi Biryani 100 g (~₹74), Badshah Biryani
skuLines.notes: Veg biryani/pulao is a standard langar and function dish — keep a vegetarian-labelled blend as the lead facing.

skuLines.line: Paneer and curry-base masalas (shahi paneer, kadai paneer, matar paneer)
skuLines.examples: MDH Shahi Paneer, Everest Kadai Paneer, Badshah Paneer Masala
skuLines.notes: On a vegetarian campus paneer is the celebration protein, so paneer blends carry the weight that chicken masala carries elsewhere — index this line up, not down.

skuLines.line: South Indian powders — sambar and rasam
skuLines.examples: MTR Sambar Powder, Aachi Sambar, Everest Sambhar Masala, MTR Rasam Powder
skuLines.notes: The Trust runs 129 academies across 13 districts and a university — teaching staff and students are not all Punjabi. One sambar + one rasam facing prevents a whole cohort's wallet leaking to a town trip.

skuLines.line: Chai masala and milk masala
skuLines.examples: Everest Tea Masala, MDH Chai Masala, Vasant Chai Masala, kesar-badam milk masala (Sanjivani/Amul-type)
skuLines.packSizes: tea masala 50 g, 100 g; milk masala 100 g, 200 g
skuLines.priceBand: ₹40-90 /50 g tea masala; ₹80-200 /100 g milk masala
skuLines.seasonality: strong Oct-Mar (cold hill winter, exam months)
skuLines.notes: A cold hill campus drinks tea all day and gives children milk at night — this is a bigger line at Baru Sahib than in a plains store. Milk masala with nuts has a shorter shelf life; buy small.

skuLines.line: Achar / pickle masala and pickling kit
skuLines.examples: Pushp Achar Masala, Everest Achar Masala, Priya/Ramdev pickle masala; kit = masala + yellow rai + methi + crystal salt
skuLines.seasonality: Apr-Jun (mango/lemon/chilli pickling) — near-zero rest of year
skuLines.notes: Married-staff households pickle for the year in one 6-8 week window. Pre-built kits (masala + rai + methi + dhela salt + mustard oil) are the single highest-basket-value play in this category and must be in place by end-March.

skuLines.line: Continental / Indo-Chinese seasonings — oregano, chilli flakes, mixed herbs, peri-peri
skuLines.examples: Keya Oregano, Catch Sprinklers, Veeba/Ching's seasoning, Sprig
skuLines.notes: Maggi/pasta/pizza-toast culture among 18-25s is what drives this; high margin, tiny cube, and a classic reason a student walks off campus if it is missing. Keep it near instant noodles, not in the spice aisle.

skuLines.line: Non-vegetarian and tandoori masalas
skuLines.examples: Everest Chicken Masala, MDH Meat Masala, Everest Tandoori Masala
skuLines.notes: Flagged, not recommended blind: Baru Sahib is a Kalgidhar Trust campus whose kitchens run vegetarian menus, and stocking meat masala may be against institutional policy. Confirm with the Trust before listing; tandoori masala alone (used on paneer/soya) is the safe half of this line.

skuLines.line: Iodised free-flow table salt
skuLines.examples: Tata Salt (1 kg MRP ₹30, Aug 2026), Aashirvaad Salt, Catch Salt, Patanjali Salt, Sambhar/local
skuLines.notes: Zero-margin traffic driver and a price-image item — residents judge the whole store on it, so never price it above town. Salt is GST-exempt. In monsoon it cakes even in laminate: sell down within 60 days and don't floor-stack.

skuLines.line: Rock salt / sendha namak — crystal and powdered
skuLines.examples: Tata Sampann Sendha Namak, Patanjali Sendha Namak, loose crystal rock salt
skuLines.seasonality: peaks at both Navratris (Mar-Apr, Sep-Oct) and other fasts
skuLines.notes: Fasting demand is a hard spike with no substitute — running out during Navratri is the kind of stockout a closed township remembers. Sendha namak has also moved into everyday use, so it no longer sells only in fast weeks.

skuLines.line: Specialty salts — black salt (kala namak) and Himalayan pink salt
skuLines.examples: Tata Sampann Black Salt, Everest Kala Namak, Himalayan pink salt (Nutriorg/Urban Platter/loose)
skuLines.packSizes: kala namak 100 g, 200 g; pink salt 500 g, 1 kg
skuLines.seasonality: kala namak spikes Apr-Jun (chaat, jaljeera, aam panna) and at fasts
skuLines.notes: Pink Himalayan salt carries obvious local resonance and is a genuinely growing everyday SKU in 2026, not just a wellness item. Both cake badly — small packs only.

skuLines.line: Low-sodium / lite salt
skuLines.examples: Tata Salt Lite, Nirogam/Saffola low-sodium, Aashirvaad Low Sodium
skuLines.notes: Small unit volume but a genuine medical need for the elderly and hypertensive staff on campus — a one-facing line that prevents an unavoidable off-campus trip. Do not sell any salt for infants under 1 year.

skuLines.line: Loose crystal (dhela) salt and institutional salt bags
skuLines.examples: Loose dhela/crystal salt, 25 kg and 50 kg iodised bags (Sambhar, regional)
skuLines.packSizes: loose by kg; 25 kg, 50 kg bags
skuLines.notes: Two buyers: pickling households (crystal salt only) and the two canteens plus hostel messes. Warehouse the bags on pallets — a 50 kg salt bag on a concrete floor in a Sirmaur monsoon is a write-off.

skuLines.line: Refined white sugar (S30) — retail to institutional
skuLines.examples: Madhur, Uttam, Dhampure, Trust/local mill sugar, loose
skuLines.seasonality: spikes at every Gurpurab and Baisakhi (karah prasad is 1:1:1 atta:ghee:sugar) and in Apr-Jun (squash/sharbat)
skuLines.notes: Highest-tonnage SKU in the category and the thinnest margin — it exists to hold the basket. Packaged sugar is 5% GST post-GST-2.0 (22 Sep 2025). Build a prasad-day forecast off the Sikh calendar: karah prasad for 5,000 people consumes sugar in bag quantities, not kilos.

skuLines.line: Unrefined and speciality sugars — sulphurless, organic, brown, demerara
skuLines.examples: Dhampure Sulphurless, 24 Mantra Organic Sugar, Trust Organic, Urban Platter Demerara
skuLines.notes: The health-aware trade-up out of white sugar, and where the margin in the sugar aisle actually is. Two facings, not five.

skuLines.line: Bura / tagar / boora sugar
skuLines.examples: Loose bura, Dhampure Bura, local halwai-grade tagar
skuLines.seasonality: heavy spikes at Gurpurabs, Baisakhi, Bandi Chhor Divas, and wedding season
skuLines.notes: Prasad, panjiri, pinni and mathri all need bura, not granulated sugar. In a Sikh institution this is a must-have, not a specialty item — and it is the line most often under-indented by a plains-trained buyer.

skuLines.line: Mishri (dhaga/crystal) and patase / batasha
skuLines.examples: Loose dhaga mishri, crystal mishri, patase/batasha (local halwai supply)
skuLines.packSizes: mishri 250 g, 500 g; patase 200 g, 500 g
skuLines.seasonality: Gurpurab and religious-function peaks; year-round baseline
skuLines.notes: Directly tied to Sikh religious practice (prasad, degh distribution, sweetened water) — the sort of SKU a generic q-commerce assortment list will never surface. Patase are fragile: stock in sealed jars, expect breakage.

skuLines.line: Icing sugar, sugar cubes and 5 g sachets
skuLines.examples: Weikfield Icing Sugar, Blue Bird Icing Sugar, sugar cubes (Trust/Madhur), 5 g service sachets
skuLines.packSizes: icing 100 g, 500 g; cubes 500 g; sachet boxes of 100
skuLines.notes: Mostly a canteen, guest-house and bakery line rather than a household one. Icing sugar hard-cakes in humidity — keep it in the driest shelf you have.

skuLines.line: Tabletop sweeteners — sucralose/aspartame tablets and sachets, stevia, monk fruit
skuLines.examples: Sugar Free Gold, Sugar Free Natura, Equal, Zevic/INJIYA Stevia, Earthful MonkSweet
skuLines.packSizes: 100-500 tablet packs; 50-100 sachet boxes; stevia 100 g; monk fruit 250 g
skuLines.priceBand: ₹120-250 tablets/sachets; ₹200-420 /100 g stevia; ₹400-850 /250 g monk fruit
skuLines.notes: Diabetic and pre-diabetic staff and elderly residents have no substitute for this locally. Stock one mass tablet pack plus one stevia; monk fruit is still premium and thinly distributed in 2026. Do not let jaggery be sold as the diabetic option — jaggery's GI is ~84, higher than white sugar.

skuLines.line: Jaggery block / cube (gur)
skuLines.examples: Loose Punjabi/UP gur, Bebe Gur, Dhampure Jaggery Cubes, Patanjali Gur
skuLines.packSizes: loose by kg; 500 g, 1 kg branded; cube packs
skuLines.seasonality: very strong Nov-Feb (cold, gur-til, Lohri/Maghi); weak and risky Jun-Sep
skuLines.notes: A cold hill winter plus a Punjabi population makes gur near-staple Nov-Feb. It sweats, ferments and attracts ants above ~25°C with humidity — buy hand-to-mouth in the monsoon and load up for winter. Loose/unbranded jaggery is GST-exempt; branded is 5%.

skuLines.line: Jaggery powder / shakkar
skuLines.examples: Loose shakkar, Bebe Jaggery Powder, 24 Mantra Organic Jaggery Powder, Dhampure
skuLines.notes: Easier to measure and store than block gur, and the fastest-growing form nationally. It is also the sweetener families use for toddlers (gur-ghee-roti) where sugar is avoided — but nothing sweet, including jaggery, for infants under 1 year.

skuLines.line: Palm and date jaggery
skuLines.examples: Natural Spices Palm Jaggery, karupatti/nolen gur, Conscious Food date sugar
skuLines.notes: Premium end of the sweetener shelf; one facing. Mainly for South Indian and health-forward staff — do not carry more than a single SKU until it proves itself.

skuLines.line: Baking soda (meetha soda) and baking powder
skuLines.examples: Weikfield Baking Powder, Blue Bird Baking Powder, Arm & Hammer/local sodium bicarbonate, Urban Platter
skuLines.seasonality: year-round; festival sweets and function baking
skuLines.notes: Also bought as a cleaning agent and for softening pulses. Distinguish the two clearly at the shelf — operators and residents mix up soda and powder constantly, and the complaint lands on the store.

skuLines.line: Cornflour and custard powder
skuLines.examples: Brown & Polson Corn Flour, Weikfield Custard Powder, Blue Bird Cornflour, Bird's
skuLines.seasonality: custard lifts in summer and at functions; cornflour year-round
skuLines.notes: Cornflour is the Indo-Chinese and gravy thickener the canteens use; custard powder is a cheap dessert for a 5,000-person mess. Both cake in humidity.

skuLines.line: Vinegar — synthetic white and apple cider
skuLines.examples: Kissan/Weikfield Synthetic Vinegar, Dabur/Bragg-type ACV, American Garden ACV
skuLines.notes: White vinegar is a canteen/Indo-Chinese essential; ACV is a wellness SKU with a very different buyer. Glass bottles are a hill-freight liability — prefer PET and pack with dunnage.

skuLines.line: Instant dry yeast and bread improver
skuLines.examples: Gloripan Instant Yeast, Blue Bird Yeast, Angel Instant Yeast
skuLines.notes: Mostly a canteen/bakery and enthusiast line. Yeast is heat- and age-sensitive — buy 10 g sachets for households and keep the 500 g pack cool, or it fails and gets returned.

skuLines.line: Food colours and essences — vanilla, kewra, rose water, elaichi essence
skuLines.examples: Bush/Weikfield food colour, Bush Vanilla Essence, Dabur/Hamdard Gulab Jal, Keva Kewra Water
skuLines.packSizes: colour 10-100 g; essence 20-30 ml; rose/kewra water 100-200 ml
skuLines.notes: Tiny cube, high margin, and indispensable when a household or the langar kitchen makes sweets. Only FSSAI-permitted synthetic colours — an unlabelled loose colour is the one item in this lane that can create a real food-safety incident.

skuLines.line: Ginger-garlic paste (and green chilli paste)
skuLines.examples: Dabur Hommade Ginger Garlic Paste, Ching's, Mother's Recipe, Priya
skuLines.notes: The single biggest time-saver for working married staff. Once opened it needs refrigeration and it is the one line in this category with a real spoilage/complaint risk — watch dates, keep the 1 kg pack for the canteens only.

skuLines.line: Kitchen chemistry — citric acid (nimbu sat), papad khar, alum (phitkari), cooking soda
skuLines.examples: Loose citric acid, papad khar (sajji), phitkari, Urban Platter citric acid
skuLines.notes: Small-value items nobody plans a trip for but everyone needs mid-recipe — exactly the stockout that sends a household to town for one ₹25 packet. Label these clearly; they are non-obvious to a young operator.

skuLines.line: Loose weighed spice counter — buy-by-gram on the top 12 spices
skuLines.examples: Loose jeera, dhania, haldi, sabut mirch, elaichi, laung, methi, rai, ajwain, saunf, anardana, til
skuLines.packSizes: any weight from 50 g; typical ticket 100-500 g
skuLines.marginBand: 15-30% (the best gross margin in the category)
skuLines.notes: The margin engine: loose/weighed goods run 15-30% against 2-8% on branded staples, and hill households prefer buying spices by weight. Needs a Legal-Metrology-verified scale and disciplined tare — a few grams' generosity per weighing compounds into real money. If you repack into your own labelled pouches you become a 'deemed manufacturer': FSSAI repacker licence plus Legal Metrology declarations (net quantity, MRP, packer details) are mandatory.

skuLines.line: Institutional bulk masala packs for canteens, messes and langar
skuLines.examples: 1 kg / 5 kg pouches of haldi, mirch, dhania, garam masala; 5-10 kg jeera; 25-50 kg salt and sugar
skuLines.priceBand: ₹550-950 /kg garam masala; ₹900-1,700 /5 kg turmeric; ₹1,800-2,900 /5 kg chilli
skuLines.seasonality: term-linked; big lift at Gurpurabs and functions
skuLines.notes: Two canteens plus hostel messes feeding ~5,000 people are the largest single customer in this category — a monthly indent contract at 5-12% on volume beats losing the account to a Nahan/Solan wholesaler. Keep this as a separate price list from retail so the two do not cannibalise.

trends2026: Clean label has crossed from premium claim to baseline expectation — 'no artificial colour / natural oils retained' (Tata Sampann, Catch low-temperature grinding) is now table stakes, and blended masalas are the fastest-growing sub-segment of a ~₹2.2 lakh-crore Indian spice market growing ~10% CAGR.

GST 2.0 (effective 22 Sep 2025) collapsed food into mainly 5%/18%: packaged spices and sugar sit at a uniform 5%, salt stays exempt, and loose/unbranded jaggery stays exempt while branded jaggery is 5% — a live pricing and labelling difference between the loose counter and the packed shelf.

Specialty salts have gone everyday: sendha namak, kala namak and Himalayan pink salt now sell outside fasting weeks, and low-sodium salt is growing on blood-pressure awareness rather than on wellness marketing.

Jaggery powder (shakkar) is displacing block gur and eating into white sugar, alongside sulphurless and organic sugar — but the 'jaggery is diabetic-safe' claim is false (GI ~84, above white sugar) and should not be repeated at the counter.

Tabletop sweeteners have gone mainstream beyond the diabetic shelf: sucralose/stevia are widely distributed, monk fruit is arriving but still premium and thin — the global stevia market is compounding ~5.5% into the 2030s.

Regional and D2C masala houses (Pushp, Goldiee, Badshah, Ramdev) are upgrading processing and taking share — the five biggest national brands together are still under 30% of the market, so a nationals-only spice rack under-serves a regional population.

Western and Indo-Chinese seasonings — oregano, chilli flakes, mixed herbs, peri-peri sprinklers — are now standard in any youth-heavy assortment, sold next to noodles and pasta rather than in the spice aisle.
Low-unit-price packs (₹5-₹10 sachets, 25-50 g shakers) keep growing: they suit cash-light students and, in a high-humidity location, cut the clumping write-off that kills a 500 g pack.
adjacentServices: Grind-to-order service: households bring or buy whole red chilli, turmeric, coriander and get it ground on the spot — the strongest trust-builder in a closed township (it visibly rules out adulteration) and a service fee on top of the goods margin.

Pickle-season kit and pre-book (Mar-Jun): mango/lemon/chilli achar kits bundling achar masala, yellow rai, methi dana, crystal dhela salt and mustard oil, sold against advance bookings so the buy is right the first time.

Prasad and festival kits keyed to the Sikh calendar: pre-portioned karah prasad packs (atta : desi ghee : sugar in 1:1:1), bura, mishri and patase for Gurpurabs, Baisakhi and Bandi Chhor Divas; gur-til bundles for Lohri and Maghi in January.

Canteen / mess / langar supply contract: a separate monthly indent price list in 1 kg, 5 kg, 25 kg and 50 kg packs for the two canteens and the hostel kitchens, with a fixed delivery day to the warehouse.

Own-label repack of loose spices into 100 g / 200 g pouches at a better margin than branded — requires an FSSAI repacker (deemed-manufacturer) licence and Legal Metrology declarations, so treat it as a project, not a shelf change.

Monsoon storage attach: airtight jars, food-grade containers and silica sachets merchandised beside the spice shelf from June, plus a 'we store it dry' claim on the loose counter — spice powders can pick up ~12% of their weight in moisture in 48 hours at high humidity.
WhatsApp / campus indent and home delivery for married staff quarters with infants and for elderly residents, so a ₹25 forgotten packet never becomes a 30-50 km trip to Nahan or Solan.

Standing monsoon and winter buffer stock (6-8 weeks of non-perishable spices, salt and sugar) as an explicit service promise to residents — the hill road into Rajgarh is the real constraint, not the supplier.
